nodes.label: YouTube API Credentials Setup
nodes.rationale: Two APIs must be enabled: YouTube Data API v3 for uploading, metadata, public statistics and trends, and YouTube Analytics API for watch time, subscribers gained and estimated revenue - without the second, uploads still work but statistics show only public counters. The OAuth client must be type 'Web application', not 'Desktop app', because the bot receives the callback in a browser. Consent-screen scopes can be left empty since the application requests its scopes at runtime.

nodes.label: redirect_uri_mismatch (Error 400)
nodes.rationale: The single most common setup failure. The URI registered in Google Cloud must match PUBLIC_BASE_URL + /accounts/oauth/callback/youtube character for character: https vs http, no trailing slash, same host (www. counts as different), matching port. Because it is so easy to get subtly wrong, the application's own Accounts page displays the exact string to paste.

nodes.label: YouTube API Daily Quota
nodes.rationale: 10,000 units per day per project, ~1,600 units per upload, so roughly six uploads per day regardless of how many channels are connected. Reading statistics costs 1 unit per call covering up to 50 videos, so collection and trend research are effectively free. The quota resets at midnight Pacific time and the bot marks the job retryable rather than failed, so it resumes automatically with no operator action. More headroom means a quota increase or a separate Google Cloud project per channel.

nodes.label: Ubuntu Automatic Install
nodes.rationale: deploy/install_ubuntu.sh --domain --email performs eleven steps in order: packages, socialbot system user, directory layout, virtualenv, .env with fresh SECRET_KEY and ENCRYPTION_KEY locked to mode 600, init-db plus a random administrator password, both systemd units, nginx, Let's Encrypt with HTTP->HTTPS redirect, ufw, and finally flask check. The generated admin password is printed once and stored nowhere.

nodes.label: Ubuntu Manual Install
nodes.rationale: Offered for people who want to understand each step or whose environment the installer does not fit - a different init system, a shared host, an existing nginx setup. The shipped systemd and nginx templates contain @PLACEHOLDER@ tokens that must be substituted.

nodes.label: Two systemd Services (Web and Worker)
nodes.rationale: gunicorn runs three worker processes. If each of them started the scheduler, three copies would plan the same upload and the video would be published three times. The web service therefore runs with SCHEDULER_ENABLED=0, and worker.py - a single process - owns the schedule.

nodes.label: Dedicated System User with No Login Shell
nodes.rationale: A dedicated system user with no shell means that if the web application is ever compromised, the attacker lands on an account that cannot log in and can only write to three directories (data/, media/, logs/) - enforced further by the systemd ReadWritePaths= line.

nodes.label: Let's Encrypt TLS with certbot
nodes.rationale: certbot --nginx --redirect is what adds the HTTP->HTTPS redirect the PRD asks for; certbot rewrites the nginx site file in place. Certificates last 90 days and certbot.timer renews at 30 days remaining. The DNS A record must already point at the server before installing, because Let's Encrypt verifies ownership over port 80. The ACME challenge location must stay reachable over plain HTTP or renewal fails.

nodes.label: Windows Server Setup
nodes.rationale: Windows has no gunicorn, so waitress-serve runs the web tier and NSSM registers SocialBotWeb and SocialBotWorker as services (exactly one worker instance, for the same reason as the systemd split). The application does not terminate TLS itself, so either IIS with URL Rewrite plus ARR or nginx for Windows fronts it; the proxy must forward HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO=https with BEHIND_PROXY=1 or the app redirects in a loop. Antivirus real-time scanning of media\ noticeably slows ffmpeg.

nodes.label: Test Server Setup
nodes.rationale: For evaluating on a laptop or internal VM with no domain and no certificate: FORCE_HTTPS=0 and BEHIND_PROXY=0 because there is no TLS and no proxy, and SCHEDULER_ENABLED=1 because a single process can safely own the schedule. Google refuses plain http redirect URIs for public hosts but does allow http://localhost, which is what makes the full connect flow testable locally. ENCRYPTION_KEY must still be a real Fernet key - it cannot be faked. Setting Default privacy to private or unlisted exercises the whole pipeline without anything appearing on the channel.

nodes.label: SQLite URL Slash Convention
nodes.rationale: sqlite:///relative/path is relative while sqlite:////absolute/path is absolute - an absolute DATABASE_URL takes four slashes. Getting this wrong surfaces as sqlite3.OperationalError: unable to open database file.

nodes.label: Moving to PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: Worth it above a few thousand videos or when concurrent writers are needed. Switch DATABASE_URL to postgresql+psycopg and re-run init-db - note that init-db creates an empty schema and does not migrate existing SQLite data, which needs a tool such as pgloader.

nodes.label: OAuth Testing Mode 7-Day Token Expiry
nodes.rationale: While the OAuth consent screen sits in 'Testing' mode only listed test users may authorise the app and their refresh tokens expire after 7 days, which presents as a connection that works and then silently breaks a week later. Clicking 'Publish app' fixes it; for a personal bot using only these scopes Google's verification is usually not required, so the 'unverified app' warning can be clicked through via Advanced -> Go to ... (unsafe).

nodes.label: flask check Configuration Diagnostic
nodes.rationale: The designated first move for any problem - it covers most install failures and prints the fix underneath each failure. It is also the last step the Ubuntu installer runs.

nodes.label: Troubleshooting Reference
nodes.rationale: Organised by symptom across installation/start-up, web interface, connecting a channel, uploads, video processing, statistics, trends, TLS and performance - deliberately covering 'the problems people actually hit' rather than an exhaustive error list.

nodes.label: First Run: Connect, Add, Publish
nodes.rationale: Sign in and change the password, connect the channel via Accounts -> Connect an account and confirm with Test, review the settings defaults, add a video with its rights fields set, confirm rights, then let the worker publish automatically within five minutes of the next slot or force it with the dashboard's 'Plan and run uploads'. Publishing times are UTC, not local.

nodes.label: Rights Confirmation Step
nodes.rationale: Ticking the confirmation box moves a video from draft to ready and into the pool the automation draws from. The confirming username and timestamp are written to the audit log deliberately: approving publication is the moment somebody takes responsibility for the copyright position. Rights-unverified material is blocked from publishing entirely.

nodes.label: Backups and the ENCRYPTION_KEY
nodes.rationale: Three things cannot be regenerated: .env (especially ENCRYPTION_KEY), the database, and the media files. deploy/backup.sh covers config plus database, --with-media covers everything, and it is meant to run nightly from cron. Losing ENCRYPTION_KEY makes every stored OAuth token unreadable and forces every channel to be reconnected by hand, so it must be backed up somewhere other than the server itself.

nodes.label: Upgrade Procedure
nodes.rationale: Back up first, stop both services, git pull (which keeps .env, data/ and media/), update dependencies, run flask db upgrade and flask seed-roles, restart and run flask check. seed-roles refreshes the built-in roles so permissions added in a new version reach Administrator and Editor; custom roles are deliberately left alone so an upgrade never silently widens an operator-defined role.
